TAL_AXES_BARK_SPLITTING_CAST.why: Partial: Splinter Cast or Shock Cast + Bark-Splitting Cast targets unattended map objects and explicit wooden barriers, ropes, vines and banner poles even when attended, through the thrown axe's long range at normal accuracy and adds one weapon die, using the shared object damage resolver (combat/ext/axes_bark_cast.py). Shock adds no Splinter PB damage or creature reaction condition. Lodging/Turning Cast, unidentified similar targets and Foundation restraint/creature links remain GM riders; CORE_WITH_RIDERS, not FULL.

TAL_AXES_AXE_BITES_THE_FORMATION.why: Targets a formation node, barrier panel, talisman circuit, or comparable temporary structure and rolls against a 'formation DC' or 'creator's Cultivation Save DC' the table has no representation for; this is an object/structure-only Axes Check with no fight-table equivalent.

TAL_AXES_SPLIT_THE_CHAIN.why: A cultivated Grappled/Restrained on an ally within reach: Hewing Strike: Split the Chain makes the Axes Check against the technique's save DC -- suppressed until the start of your next turn, ended on a success by 5 or more (combat/ext/axes_split_chain.py, rider lane C10). Hitting a physical restraint (rope, net) still needs restraint objects the table does not have.

TAL_AXES_FOREST_OF_FALLING_STANDARDS.why: Targets up to six banners/standards/signal drums (objects) and suppresses abstract 'command, morale, or formation benefits' tied to a Warleader command engine this table does not otherwise track as objects; the talent's own text says it is not the Warleader command engine.

TAL_AXES_FRANCISCA_OPENING.why: Lets the wielder choose two Cast Axe riders at once, or force a choice between two outcomes on a miss; the fight table's Cast Axe menu offers exactly one rider per throw and has no compound- or miss-only-choice mechanism to model either clause.

SPEAR_BASE_SPEAR_TRAINING.why: 'Gain proficiency with spears, pikes, lances, and tridents; if already proficient with all four, choose one Spear talent as a bonus talent' -- weapon proficiency and a bonus-talent pick, both build-time choices with no in-combat effect.

tianxia.talent.weapons.adaptive_arsenal.why: 'Regain Martial Focus ... if the new weapon's method is meaningfully different ... the GM may deny this if the switch is cosmetic' -- requires a GM judgment call on whether a weapon swap is meaningfully different, which this table cannot evaluate automatically.

TAL_WEAPONS_ARMAMENT_CONDUIT_INITIATE.why: Designates a proficient weapon as the character's Conduit Weapon; the talent's own text says outright it 'does not yet replace its attack and damage ability modifier' -- a build-time designation with no combat effect of its own.

tianxia.talent.weapons.armory_of_the_roa.why: A short-rest preparation ritual (which weapons count as familiar until the next long rest) -- out-of-combat logistics, no fight-table effect.

tianxia.talent.weapons.arsenal_student.why: Grants weapon proficiencies; a build-time choice, not an in-combat effect.

TAL_WEAPONS_CASTING_HAND_WEAPON_METHOD.why: Applied by the compiler (factory_compiler weapon loop, owner 2026-09-26): with Armament Conduit Initiate, the proficient weapon that gains most from the cultivation ability (_casting_ability) attacks and deals damage with it instead of Strength or Dexterity. (auto-lane4 2026-09-29: the earlier 'table' label was stale.)

tianxia.talent.weapons.long_weapon_measu.why: Adds a second Opportunity Attack trigger (a creature entering, not just leaving, the wielder's reach); this table's opportunity-attack triggering only fires on leaving reach, and the ext hook points (opportunity_allowed) can only forbid an attack, not add a new trigger condition.

TAL_WEAPONS_PROFILE_SPECIALIST.why: 'Choose one legal weapon profile specialty talent' -- a talent-pick, build-time choice with no in-combat effect of its own.

tianxia.talent.weapons.weapon_thrower_s_.why: Draw-as-part-of-attack action economy and tracking where a missed thrown weapon lands are both logistics with no HP, condition, or resource change to type.

TAL_DUAL_WIELDING_CRITICAL_FOLLOW_UP.why: New owned rows use native pre-damage 19–20 critical range for a Paired Strike with a readied Qualifying Pair; historical rows stay deferred.

TAL_DUAL_WIELDING_DUAL_DRAW.why: Lets the wielder equip or unequip two one-handed weapons wherever the rules allow equipping or unequipping one -- pure hand/inventory logistics with no HP, condition, or resource change to type.

TAL_DUAL_WIELDING_DUAL_OPPORTUNITY.why: Doubles the attack count of the generic Opportunity Attack reaction via the same extra_attacks mechanism Cleaving Arc (Axes) uses; see reviewed_final.d/martial.json.

TAL_DUAL_WIELDING_FOCUSING_DEFENSE.why: Dodge adds two AC while a Qualifying Pair is readied. Losing the pair removes the increase; redrawing restores it until Dodge expires.

TAL_DAEMONIC_CULTIVATION_DEMONIC_TECHNIQ.why: Steals an arbitrary property (damage type, a Resistance) from whichever technique a nearby creature just used; this table does not expose an opposing ability's damage type or other properties generically to typed effects, and the reaction's own Cultivation Check contest has no opposing DC to read either.

TAL_DAEMONIC_CULTIVATION_PROFANE_BREAKTH.why: 'During a cultivation session, you may accept daemonic pressure to increase the result of one Breakthrough, cultivation meditation, or CXP-related check' -- a downtime activity outside combat.

TAL_DAEMONIC_CULTIVATION_INNER_DEMON_INC.why: A once-per-long-rest stance with several clauses this table cannot express as simple typed effects (Fly Speed without Hover, attacks 'count as magical', Daemonic Augment usable twice per turn on different rolls, an extra Devoured Essence once per round); only Resistance to Necrotic/Psychic and the end-of-incarnation Corruption gain are typed. Left for an owner ruling on which clauses matter enough to hand-build given how rarely a once-per-long-rest ability recurs in a single fight.

PRESSURE_POINTS_BASE_PRESSURE_POINTS_TRA.why: Grants proficiency, a bonus talent pick, and four specific known talents when the sphere is learned -- all build-time choices with no in-combat effect.

TAL_DEATH_GHOSTLY_RETINUE.why: A 1-hour Ritual Procedure with an 8-hour duration, prepared before a fight, not a combat action.

TAL_DEATH_QUIET_BURIAL.why: A Multi-Mode rite over a corpse/grave object: ending a haunting, preventing animation, quieting destroyed undead remains, or granting a tracking check -- all out-of-fight logistics. Its one borderline combat clause ('let one dying creature within reach immediately make a death saving throw with Advantage') is a single-use battlefield mercy with no separate typed effect this pass; GM runs it as a normal death save with Advantage if chosen.

TAL_DEATH_DEATH_MASK.why: A 1-hour 'appear dead' disguise contested by a Medicine check or direct examination -- this table has no passive detection-contest mechanic to pit the target's Advantage against an examiner's check.

TAL_DEATH_GHOST_LANTERN.why: A persistent, independently-movable Tiny object with its own AC/HP/light radius and detection buffs; this table's zones/summons model areas and creatures, not a freestanding movable light source with its own statline, so this was not built this pass.

TAL_DEATH_GRAVE_MERIDIAN_AWAKENING.why: A bundle of passive upgrades to other talents (Grave Sense range, Withering Hand's damage-type choice, incorporeal targeting, an undead-asset free move) with no single discrete effect of its own; upgrading each named talent individually was not reached this pass.

TAL_DEATH_COURT_OF_THE_NINTH_GRAVE.why: A multi-clause 30-foot Domain (automatic detection, Necrotic Resistance for self and allies, ally Advantage on death saves, terrain-ignoring servant movement, plus an on-turn trigger the text cuts off before); this table's aura/zone tooling could model pieces of it, but the full bundle was not built this pass.

TAL_DEATH_BONE_BASTION.why: A conjured barrier object with its own AC/HP/Cover and Temporary HP; combat/rules/walls.json (new on integrate/0929, not yet reviewed by this worker) may be the right tool for a follow-up pass, but building it was not reached this pass.

tianxia.talent.disease.hidden_carrier.why: A passive defense against an opposing creature's own Diagnose-style check/Medicine check/divination against the wielder (a Cultivation Check contest initiated by someone else, not a fight-table action this character takes); this table has no generic 'resist being diagnosed' contest to run automatically.

tianxia.talent.disease.narrow_quarantine.why: Already typed and compiling correctly (a 5-foot Concentration-free variant of Raise the Quarantine Veil's area); reviewed, no fix needed.

tianxia.talent.disease.physician_of_bad_.why: Grants one additional GM-answered question when using Diagnose the Sickness (itself already labelled outside/informational); pure information, no HP/condition/resource effect.

tianxia.talent.disease.plague_needle.why: Delivers Sow the Fever Seed's Disease damage 'through' a separate weapon attack's own hit result, folding two attacks' worth of typed effects into one roll; this table's attack pipeline resolves one ability's effects at a time and has no hook to borrow another ability's hit result mid-resolution.

SABERS_BASE_SABER_LINE_METHOD.why: A passive weapon-profile/proficiency choice with GM adjudication of legal saber profiles, not a combat action.

TAL_FENCING_READ_FOE.why: Grants Insight proficiency or Expertise -- a character-build skill choice, not a combat effect.
